This pathway provides a clear, mechanistic link between Dexfosfoserine and the cyclin B1 protein, highlighting a potential role in the regulation of the G2 phase of the cell cycle. The presence of multiple paths with similar target relationships supports the idea that Quisqualic acid acts as a bridge between Dexfosfoserine and cyclin B1, possibly through a common intermediary. The integration of these pathways underscores the importance of Quisqualic acid in mediating the effects of Dexfosfoserine on cyclin B1, suggesting a potential role in cell cycle regulation.
